_comment: The broker's roster. It is a CONFIGURATION, not a state store: the broker never writes a reading into it and never keeps a heartbeat. `baseUrl` is the node's gate (docs/mesh/71-mesh-program.md §2.1: the capacity surface lives in the gate, which is what `tailscale serve` publishes), and the broker appends /mesh/capacity. NAMES ARE TAILSCALE DNS LABELS, not host names and not ssh aliases: §2.1's invariant is node == fqdn.split('.')[0], the gate answers that label, and lib/config.js now REFUSES to boot on a roster row that breaks it (see its header). Measured 2026-09-16 23:31Z: the laptop's Self.HostName is `zabz-yoga` but its DNS name is `zabz-yoga-1`, and `zabz-yoga` does not resolve at all.
_transport_comment: Every row carries `dispatch`: can this node ACCEPT v1 work (`ssh <alias> dsh --profile headless`)? Three states, never collapsed: true = measured to work, false = measured not to (the evidence says how), null = never measured. The broker ranks false below true, prints the fact in the rationale, and still places there when it is the only candidate (queue, never amputate). docs/mesh/76-broker.md §10.4 has the finding.

dispatch.evidence: RE-MEASURED WORKING 2026-10-08, after the defect in this row's previous revision was found and fixed. THE DEFECT: scripts/vscode-update/mcp_launcher.py opened data/logs/mcp-launcher.log UNCONDITIONALLY after computing `missing = [keys absent from the repo .env]`; under the mesh child's execution context that open raised PermissionError, the one-shot exited 1 with no completion frame, and because the retry classifier read ANY non-zero exit with no frame as `child-ran-transport-fault` (harvest, never re-dispatch) NOTHING EVER REROUTED. Eight of eight children died here while zabz-tech-linux sat idle, and every session silently went local. THE FIX, in two halves, both committed: (1) the launcher now routes every log open through `_open_log()`, which returns a write-nothing stand-in instead of raising, because a server must not depend on being able to log (the node's copy is backed up as mcp_launcher.py.bak-prelogfix); (2) plugin-remote-fanout/lib/retry-plan.js now answers `node-specific` - i.e. reroute - for a non-zero exit that produced NOTHING AT ALL, while keeping the anti-duplication guard intact for any child that emitted its own markers. VERIFIED AFTER THE FIX, over ssh: `node <bin.js> --profile headless 'Reply with exactly MESH-OK-ZABZTECH and nothing else.'` -> MESH-OK-ZABZTECH, exit 0. Interpreter form and credential source unchanged.

Re-measure before changing this flag: ~/bin/mesh-node-probe.sh runs a real child turn against every node and flags any disagreement with this roster.

dispatch.evidence: MEASURED WORKING FOR v1 AGAIN, 2026-10-09, AT THE DISPATCHER'S OWN PRECONDITION - AND THE 2026-10-08 REVISION OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG TO CERTIFY ON PROBE-ONLY EVIDENCE. (1) THE DATED FAILURE, read twice. ~/bin/mesh-node-probe.sh recorded zabz-yoga-1 ok=false exit 1 6000 ms at 2026-10-08T23:15:20Z (the only failing row). Cause, from the child's own stderr: C:\Users\ezabz\.dsh\.credentials.yaml carried two stray TOP-LEVEL keys (LPT_VERIFICATION_EMAIL, LPT_VERIFICATION_PASSWORD - an LPT production verification login parked there at 23:10:19Z); credentials-local REJECTS an unknown top-level key, so the whole store failed to load and the one-shot died `dsh: MISSING_CREDENTIAL`. Repaired 23:39:43Z by indenting both keys under the existing `refs:` mapping (backup .credentials.yaml.bak-straykeys-20261008T233942Z); a real headless child turn then returned MESH-PROBE-OK, exit 0. (2) WHAT THE PROBE COULD NOT SEE, and the reason the 23:47:56Z revision was still wrong: the DISPATCHER refused the node. `mesh-run.mjs -DshBin <dsh> -Node zabz-yoga-1` exits 1 at phase=traversal with `this node's sshd session cannot traverse a reparse point (2 of 5 link(s) :: ...\profiles\node_modules\accepts)`. The probe runs a bare one-shot and never exercises probeTraversal, so a green probe is NOT evidence that a dispatch can be placed - that gap is what let a true row stand over a refused node. (3) THE MEASURED CAUSE, 2026-10-09T00:27Z, full audit of <DSH_HOME>/profiles: 492 junctions, 150 unreadable - 83 whose target provably no longer exists under _npx\1e7f6d9597241db0\node_modules (stale entries from an older install generation, which healProfilesModuleFallback never repairs because they fall outside the current closure) and 67 whose target exists but which fail in the OS's own words, `The path cannot be traversed because it contains an untrusted mount point` - the 70-remote-fanout-proof.md 4.4 reparse-point condition, RECURRED. (4) THE REPAIR, 00:27:36Z, run INSIDE an ssh session: the 83 provably-dangling links reaped (manifest C:\Users\ezabz\.dsh\profiles-links-repair-20261009T002707Z.txt) and the 67 untrusted links recreated with the same target (67 relinked, 0 failed). Verified: 409 junctions, 409/409 traversable over the node's own sshd, and probeTraversal - the dispatcher's own precondition - now answers `MESH-TRAVERSAL=OK existing 5 of 5 link(s) traversable` from the authority (00:28:16Z) and from zabz-tech (00:28:53Z). (5) WHY THIS ROW READS true: the value is now measured at the dispatcher's precondition as well as by the probe; 76-broker.md 5 item 15 is that a capability is a dated measurement, written back the same hour it is proven. SET BACK TO false if a real `mesh-run -Node zabz-yoga-1` stops getting past phase=traversal. The three ways this node has actually failed: an unknown top-level key in .credentials.yaml; untrusted reparse-point junctions under profiles (relink them INSIDE an ssh session - a relink from a local session is a no-op); and stale dangling profile links into a pruned npx cache.

nodes.note: the owner's laptop, 16c/22t. The name is `zabz-yoga-1`, not `zabz-yoga`: Self.HostName is zabz-yoga but Self.DNSName - the only name that resolves - is zabz-yoga-1 (measured 2026-09-16 23:31Z). RECURRENCES of the untrusted-reparse-point defect: 2026-09-16 (S6 relinked 413 links in-session) and 2026-10-09 (67 relinked, 83 stale reaped). Both remedies were a relink performed INSIDE an ssh session. The probe's own one-shot CANNOT see this class of failure - only mesh-run's probeTraversal can - so this row's regression test is a real dispatch, not the probe.

dispatch.evidence: MEASURED WORKING FOR v1 THROUGH THE CORRECTED INVOCATION, 2026-09-17 (14:34-15:05Z) - and the previous `false` was a DISPATCHER defect wearing a node defect's clothes, not a weak machine. Read docs/mesh/102-linux-dispatch.md §4 and docs/mesh/104-node-enabled.md before changing this flag either way. (1) THE INVOCATION IS CORRECTED AND THE ROTTED PATH IS GONE: plugin-remote-fanout/lib/nodes.js now gives this node `command: 'dsh'` - the executor is invoked BY NAME - and its `driver` fallback is the version-free symlink /usr/local/bin/node -> /home/zabz/.local/node/bin/node (v22.23.2). The dead /home/zabz/.local/node-v24.12.0-linux-x64/bin/node no longer appears in the row. The executor (/usr/local/bin/dsh, installed by scripts/provision-mesh-node.sh) resolves the interpreter from $HOME and sources /etc/dsh-worker.env (root:zabz 0640, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY + DEEPINFRA_API_KEY) itself, measured to work even under `env -i` with HOME unset and no key in the environment. The two conditions 98 §4.2 named are therefore BOTH met: the dispatcher table is corrected AND the credential reaches the dispatch process - the second by USING the executor rather than by exporting a key into an ssh session. (2) A REAL CHILD WAS DISPATCHED THROUGH THE WHOLE DISPATCHER AND RETURNED: `node bin/mesh-run.mjs -Prompt '<run hostname and reply with exactly what it printed>' -Node zabz-tech-linux` -> exit 0 in 22.6 s, framed, `MESH-HOST: zabz-tech-linux`, childHosts ["zabz-tech-linux"], disagreements [], outcome completed (102 §4 run 2; the child's own stderr shows it ran the command rather than guessing). (3) THE SAME COMMAND BEFORE THE FIX EXITED 1 with `only 0 MESH-HOST lines for 1 children`; the child's own report was `sh: 6: /home/zabz/.local/node-v24.12.0-linux-x64/bin/node: not found` (exit 127, 102 §1). (4) The stale 2026-09-16 note that this node 'has no Node runtime yet' is FALSE and is corrected here: the machine has node v22.23.2, dsh 0.1.5-rc.1, a populated headless profile, and it accepts a real v1 child turn. (5) THE FLAG TAKES EFFECT IN PLACEMENT: a live `POST /place {fleet, 2 children}` puts this node in the eligible pool and places it `tier=fits` with `blockedBy: []` when it is the only candidate, where `v1: false` produced `tier=transport` with `blockedBy: ["transport"]` (docs/mesh/104-node-enabled.md). SET BACK TO false if the executor form is replaced by an explicit interpreter pair again, or if /usr/local/bin/dsh or /etc/dsh-worker.env is removed from the node - re-measure, do not re-argue.
